title: Repair station cards and teacher-written practice extract
subject: English Language
source: Seeded from english-language/y11 lesson 53 (Repair station cards and teacher-written practice extract (pupil PDF))
intro: Read the text carefully. Annotate it: underline key words and write your ideas in the margin.

passage.title: Teacher-written practice extract for TGA
paras: The library closed at six, but nobody told the rain. It kept on, steady and grey, as the last readers buttoned their coats. Inside, the lights went off one row at a time, like a house putting its children to bed.
Then, at the very end of the hall, one lamp stayed on. Under it sat a boy with a dictionary, his finger moving slowly down the page, as if the words might run away.

questions.q: Station work, part 1: complete your station's task on the fresh extract.
questions.a: Station 1: five effect sentences. Station 2: a map of shifts (closing, lights off, one lamp, the boy) with two explanations. Station 3: comparison of this extract with Text One 'Why I Walk' (noticing small things).
questions.model: Teacher models one example per station: effect ('like a house putting its children to bed' makes the library tender and safe); structure (the final zoom to one lamp); comparison (both writers notice small details that others pass by).

questions.q: in the portal response box, write one full answer paragraph for your station's question on the fresh extract. Starter: 'The writer...'
questions.a: A paragraph that clearly shows the repaired skill.
questions.model: Structure station: 'The writer structures the extract like a camera closing in: the whole building, then the rows of lights going off, then one lamp and one boy. This narrowing makes the boy's quiet determination the emotional centre.'

questions.q: swap and check with a partner from the same station.
write a second paragraph using a different skill.
